facts.text: Ossington Avenue takes its name from the Denison family’s ancestral home in Nottingham, England.
The southern end of the street, known as the Ossington Strip, has long been a hub for restaurants, bars, and nightlife.
A bus route on Ossington connects directly to the Toronto Transit Commission’s Line 2 Bloor–Danforth subway station at Ossington.
In the 1880s, the stretch that is now Ossington Avenue was originally part of the planned Dundas Street, running north from Dundas to Bloor.
Ossington Avenue today runs roughly 3 kilometres north from Dundas to Bloor, with the northern section remaining largely residential.
During the late 19th century, the area around Ossington was a centre of Toronto’s meat‑packing industry, with slaughterhouses and stockyards just east of the street.
